description: NaPTAN (National Public Transport Access Nodes) is the national dataset of every point where people can access public transport in Great Britain. It covers bus, rail, tram, metro and underground stops and stations, airports and ferry terminals. The Department for Transport publishes it. Coverage is national. The data are updated daily and free under the Open Government Licence, and they can be downloaded in CSV or XML from the NaPTAN site or through the access-nodes API, and a new NaPTAN site is in beta. Caveats: the service is moving to the new site, so links and download options may change, and access points change daily. NaPTAN supports building public transport networks for flow and accessibility models, exposure of stops and stations to hazards, and emergency response planning. It complements the Bus Open Data Service and the GB accessibility indicators catalogued here.
